principle: One canonical rule source, model-scoped exceptions, and regression-backed changes. A local fix must not weaken another invariant.

rules.canonical: Each shot has one dominant camera intention. A simple shot normally uses one clear move or a locked camera. A composite move is allowed only when its phases form one causal camera sentence with an explicit trigger, path, hand-off, and landing; do not stack unrelated moves.
forbidden_legacy: Every shot has exactly one primary camera move
One primary camera move per shot
must never stack multiple moves

rules.canonical: World state is authoritative. Screen position is a camera-dependent projection and may change when the camera changes even if the subject does not move.
forbidden_legacy: screen side can never change when world position is unchanged

rules.canonical: A transition event authorizes only its participants and affected prop or scene key. Relational transactions name actor, target, prop, and hands when known.
forbidden_legacy: global event authorizes all entities

rules.canonical: Shot-detail requirements follow shot function; there is no universal per-shot checklist.
forbidden_legacy: Every shot must contain environment pressure, body micro-action, and sound anchor

rules.canonical: A new shot advances at least one meaningful state dimension. Major reversals should usually advance two or more, but tactical or insert shots do not need a forced emotional change.
forbidden_legacy: Every new shot must reveal both a new fact and a new emotional level

rules.canonical: Model-specific defects and workarounds apply only to the named model/interface unless independently verified elsewhere.
forbidden_legacy: prefer them even on other models

rules.canonical: Asset names are stable internal identity keys. Render @Name only on interfaces that support @ reference binding.
forbidden_legacy: every named asset has a reference image

rules.canonical: Operational claims are tagged as official, controlled, field-observed, partial, inferred, or experimental; unverified observations do not become universal hard rules.

User-facing planning/explanation follows the user language. A model adapter may require a different machine-facing grammar or field language when that requirement is current and evidenced; that adapter-level syntax wins only for the compiled machine prompt.
forbidden_legacy: Use Chinese shot numbering
Use concise, causal Chinese descriptions
Use chronological, causal Chinese prose

rules.canonical: Preserve supplied dialogue verbatim and in order. A line may cross cuts when audio is continuous, the cut does not restart or duplicate words, and the target workflow supports it; across independently generated clips use an explicit audio handoff or keep the line intact.
forbidden_legacy: Do not split a line across shots
A line longer than four seconds stays in one continuous shot

rules.canonical: Do not translate an abstract emotion or power label directly into a camera angle/move. Camera and blocking choices must be justified by visible action, spatial relation, information order, or a deliberate inversion.
forbidden_legacy: 角色占上风 → 镜头**仰视**他
角色处下风 → 镜头**俯视**他

rules.canonical: UI safe areas are platform/interface specific. Use a current user/platform safe-area template when available; otherwise keep critical story information away from likely overlay edges without claiming universal percentages.
forbidden_legacy: top 8% / bottom 15% / right 12%
central 70%
central 85%

rules.canonical: Generic planning language never overrides a verified model-specific machine grammar. Keep the director plan model-neutral, then compile it through the selected adapter; adapter syntax overrides only the machine-facing prompt layer.

Exact model capabilities, syntax requirements, limits, and defect workarounds require a dated provenance entry. Undocumented prompt-length/action/noun-count formulas remain heuristics or are removed; volatile interface limits defer to the current interface.
forbidden_legacy: Keep 1–3 actions maximum
more than ~4–5 distinct nouns breaks it
Single take: **40–80 words**
image-to-video: 20–40
